patch.value:
## What shipped and what did not
The attribution-enforcement work delivered strict unknown-author rejection, SDK test-all author parity, and a public acknowledgeUnknownAuthorHistoryEvents primitive with hardened error handling. Its acceptance criteria also stated that the five stranded events would be dispositioned and health would return ok:true. The primitive exists; the disposition was never executed against this repository, and there is no CLI or MCP path to execute it.

## Why the disposition is a judgement call
Acknowledgment records a reviewer, an attributed author, and a reason against immutable events. That is a maintainer decision about who is accountable for five specific historical mutations, not a mechanical cleanup, which is why it must be run deliberately rather than folded into a sweep.

## Boundary
No history rewriting. No baseline movement. No hand-attribution of legacy pre-baseline events — only the five post-baseline actionable ones. Preventing future unknown-author events is the harness identity work, not this item.
Execute and expose the unknown-author acknowledgment flow: dispose the five stranded events and give the shipped SDK primitive a CLI and MCP surface

The five 2026-07-16 unknown-author test_run_track events carry an audited acknowledgment with reviewer, attributed author, and reason, recorded without rewriting history or moving the baseline; pm health returns ok:true and validate no longer reports validate_history_unknown_author_events for this workspace; acknowledgeUnknownAuthorHistoryEvents is reachable from the CLI and from MCP with the same typed errors as the SDK primitive, wired through every required registration site; Docs state when acknowledgment is appropriate and that it is a recorded disposition, never a way to attribute authorship after the fact
Every validate and health warning maps to an open item, and the acknowledgment capability is reachable without writing SDK code

The acknowledgment flow shipped as an SDK primitive and was never run against this repository, so pm health has reported ok:false continuously since 2026-07-16 and the workspace's own governance signal is permanently degraded.
Restores health to a trustworthy binary signal instead of a known-red one that reviewers learn to ignore, and removes the last validate warning with no open owner.
The five stranded events carry an audited disposition, pm health returns ok:true, and acknowledgment is invocable from the CLI and MCP rather than only from TypeScript.

The attribution-enforcement item closed on the strength of the primitive existing; the repo-side execution half was never scheduled, which is the same shipped-but-not-adopted pattern the merge-safety adoption work already hit once.

message: File repo-side execution and CLI exposure of the unknown-author acknowledgment flow
